title: Pediatric GI, Part 3: Lower GI, bleeding and liver

sections.title: Protein-losing enteropathy
notes: Serum protein lost into the gut: **edema, low albumin and low globulin**.

Causes: primary **intestinal lymphangiectasia**, Whipple disease (Tropheryma whipplei, treat with antibiotics), lymphoma, radiation, **post-Fontan**, constrictive pericarditis, heart failure, polyps, infections, IBD, milk protein allergy, Ménétrier (CMV).
**Stool alpha-1 antitrypsin** is not normally in stool, positive means protein-losing enteropathy. Treat the cause.

sections.title: Intestinal lymphangiectasia
notes: Blocked intestinal lymph drainage, usually **under 3 years**: **lymphopenia, low albumin, low globulin**.
Associated with Turner, Noonan, Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber, heart failure. Chylous ascites or effusion, steatorrhea.
Diagnosis: stool alpha-1 antitrypsin. Treat by replacing long-chain fat with **medium-chain triglycerides**.

sections.title: Short bowel syndrome
notes: Loss of over 50% of small bowel: malabsorption, TPN.
Good odds of weaning TPN: **15 cm with the ileocecal valve**, or 20 cm or more without it. Start **trophic feeds** gradually.
**Duodenum: iron, folate, calcium**. **Ileum: B12 and bile salts** (and fat-soluble vitamins).
Late complications: **oxalate kidney stones** (fat binds calcium so oxalate is absorbed), bloody diarrhea from fast feeds, constipation, bacterial overgrowth.

sections.title: Small bowel bacterial overgrowth
notes: Suspect with chronic abdominal pain after **gut surgery** or anatomic problems.
Protections lost: gastric acid, bile and pancreatic enzymes, lactobacillus, mucosal barrier, **ileocecal valve**.
Bloating, distension, diarrhea, fatigue, **ataxia**. Labs: metabolic acidosis with **high D-lactic acid**.
Treat with broad-spectrum antibiotics (metronidazole, amoxicillin-clavulanate). Complications: malabsorption, fat-soluble vitamin deficiency.

sections.title: Diarrhea clues to the bug
notes: **Reactive arthritis**: Salmonella, Shigella, Yersinia, Campylobacter, Cryptosporidium, C difficile.
**Guillain-Barré**: Campylobacter. Appendicitis mimic: **Yersinia**. IgA nephropathy: Campylobacter.
**Erythema nodosum**: Yersinia, Campylobacter, Salmonella. **Hemolytic uremic syndrome**: Shigella dysenteriae, **E coli O157:H7**.

sections.title: Dehydration: oral rehydration
notes: Case: 4-year-old, nonbloody diarrhea, mild tachycardia, normal BP and capillary refill, **drinking**: mild to moderate dehydration. **Oral rehydration solution at home**.
Oral rehydration is best for mild to moderate, **even with vomiting**, as long as the child drinks.
IV fluids only for **shock, low BP or severe dehydration**.

sections.title: Diarrhea management
notes: Viral and most bacterial diarrhea is **self-limited**, no antibiotics.
**No loperamide** (ileus, toxic megacolon, death). Bismuth risks salicylate toxicity.
Keep a **regular diet**, but **no juice or sports drinks** (osmotic). Probiotics help. Lasting over 2 weeks: try lactose-free.
Prolonged viral diarrhea causes lactose intolerance: stool **reducing substances positive, pH under 6**.

sections.title: When to give antibiotics
notes: **Shigella**: ciprofloxacin, TMP-SMX or azithromycin. Third-generation cephalosporin if admitted.
**Salmonella**: only if **under 3 months**, malignancy or immunocompromised (ceftriaxone).
**C difficile**: metronidazole, again for a recurrence. If it fails: **oral vancomycin only, never IV**.
Entamoeba: metronidazole, then a luminal agent (paromomycin or iodoquinol).

sections.title: Toddler's diarrhea
notes: Under 3 years, **lots of juice**. Up to 10 loose stools a day, **no blood or mucus**, healthy and growing, **no stools at night**, undigested food visible.
Reassure, **cut juice, add fat** to the diet.

sections.title: Secondary lactase deficiency
notes: Villous tip injury after **rotavirus**, parasites, celiac, Crohn. Gas, bloating, osmotic diarrhea.
Diagnosis: 2-week **lactose-free trial**, hydrogen breath test, stool **pH under 5 and reducing substances**. Treat lactose-free or lactase enzyme.

sections.title: Congenital diarrheas
notes: With **polyhydramnios**: congenital chloride diarrhea (**acidic stool, metabolic alkalosis, low serum chloride, high stool chloride**) and congenital sodium diarrhea (alkaline stool, metabolic acidosis, low serum sodium).
No polyhydramnios: **microvillous inclusion disease**, watery diarrhea from day 1, villous atrophy without inflammation. Lifelong TPN, intestinal transplant.

sections.title: GI bleeding: upper vs lower
notes: Hematemesis: upper. Bright red blood: lower. Melena or occult blood: either, **NG aspirate** helps.
First confirm it's blood (guaiac). Mimics: food colouring, juice, **cefdinir** (maroon stool).

sections.title: GI bleeding by age
notes: Newborn: **swallowed maternal blood** (Apt test, cracked nipples, bloody cesarean), NEC, malrotation, fissure, Hirschsprung colitis.
Infant: fissure, **milk protein colitis**, infectious colitis, intussusception, Meckel, HUS.
Older child: **check the nose first (epistaxis)**, gastritis, ulcer, varices, juvenile polyps, infectious colitis, fissure, HSP.

sections.title: GI bleeding: management and Mallory-Weiss
notes: Stabilize first. Tachycardia, hypotension, orthostatic changes, slow capillary refill: significant bleed.
Swallowed blood (nose, breastfeeding, dental work, tonsillectomy), stress ulcer, varices.
**Mallory-Weiss**: tear at the gastroesophageal junction from forceful vomiting or retching. Most heal on their own, band if persistent.

sections.title: Gastritis and varices
notes: Diffuse gastritis: trauma, burns, ICU. Localized: **NSAIDs**, alcohol, H pylori. Coffee-ground emesis.
Varices: most common pediatric cause is **portal vein cavernous transformation (thrombosis)**. Splenomegaly, ascites, jaundice.
Portal vein thrombosis risks: **umbilical venous catheter**, neonatal sepsis, shock, exchange transfusion. Secondary prevention: acid suppression, sucralfate, sclerotherapy or banding.

sections.title: Meckel diverticulum
notes: Vitelline duct remnant in the ileum with **ectopic gastric mucosa** making acid that ulcerates nearby ileum.
Rule of 2s: 2%, 2 feet from the ileocecal valve, 2 inches long, usually under 2 years.
Classic: **significant painless rectal bleeding** (Meckel until proven otherwise). Can be painful. Anemia, hypovolemia, **lead point for intussusception**, appendicitis mimic.
**Meckel (Tc-99m) scan** is the best first test, but **a negative scan doesn't rule it out** (capsule may miss it too). Treatment: surgery.

sections.title: Juvenile polyps and polyposis
notes: Most common childhood polyp, age **2 to 10**. **Bright red painless bleeding right after stooling**, may prolapse as a dark red mass. Colonoscopy and removal.
**Juvenile polyposis**: over 5 polyps, autosomal dominant. Bleeding, intussusception, failure to thrive, anemia, low albumin. Cancer risk rises with more polyps or family history.

sections.title: Gardner syndrome
notes: Autosomal dominant: **polyps with osteomas**, epidermoid cysts, dental abnormalities. Polyps are premalignant (small bowel, colon, stomach).

sections.title: Liver tests: what they mean
notes: **PT and albumin are the true liver function tests**. PT prolonged and **not fixed by IV vitamin K** means liver failure.
AST and ALT can be in the thousands with a healthy liver (virus, acetaminophen). They are the most sensitive markers of hepatocyte damage, not function.
Any **direct hyperbilirubinemia is pathologic**: cholestasis, biliary atresia.
High AST and ALT from muscle: **Duchenne**, check **CK**.
**Shrinking liver, falling AST and ALT, rising PT** that doesn't correct with vitamin K: liver failure, transplant.

sections.title: Alkaline phosphatase and GGT
notes: High ALP: obstructive liver disease, **growth spurts**, **rickets**, fractures, **transient hyperphosphatasemia of infancy**, bowel disease.
**High ALP with normal GGT: bone, not liver**. GGT doesn't rise in bone disease, is normally high in newborns.

sections.title: Causes of jaundice
notes: Unconjugated: hemolysis, Gilbert, Crigler-Najjar, **hypothyroidism**, UTI and sepsis.

Conjugated: infection (TORCH, **UTI**, sepsis), metabolic (**alpha-1 antitrypsin, CF, galactosemia**), obstructive (**biliary atresia, choledochal cyst**), Alagille, PFIC, hypothyroidism, TPN, shock and heart failure.

sections.title: Gilbert vs Crigler-Najjar
notes: **Gilbert**: low UGT, mild indirect bilirubin **under 5**, worse with **fasting, fever, exercise**. Reassure.
**Crigler-Najjar type 1**: **no UGT**, bilirubin 20 to 50, day 1, **kernicterus**. Phototherapy, then liver transplant.
Type 2: partial UGT, bilirubin 7 to 20, well. Reassure (responds to phenobarbital).

sections.title: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
notes: **Most common genetic cause of liver disease in children**. Prolonged jaundice and neonatal hepatitis, hepatomegaly.
Later: portal hypertension, varices, cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma in adults. Confirm with liver biopsy and phenotype.

sections.title: Wilson disease
notes: Autosomal recessive copper buildup in **liver and brain**. Think of it with **unexplained liver disease plus neuro or psychiatric change** (depression, psychosis, school decline).
Tremor, dysarthria, dystonia, **Kayser-Fleischer rings**, **hemolytic anemia** can be first.
**Low ceruloplasmin (under 20)**, urine copper over 100 µg/day, liver biopsy. Treat: low copper diet, **penicillamine**. Fatal if missed.

sections.title: Neonatal cholestasis
notes: Most common cause in preemies: **TPN**. Most common congenital infection: **CMV**.
**Jaundice still present at 2 weeks: check direct bilirubin**. Pale or clay stools and hepatomegaly add concern.
Workup: direct bilirubin, AST, ALT, **ALP and GGT (obstruction)**, urinalysis and culture, **urine reducing substances and eye exam for cataract (galactosemia)**, CF and thyroid screen.
Advanced injury: **PT not corrected by vitamin K**, high ammonia, low albumin, hypoglycemia.

sections.title: Biliary atresia
notes: Obliteration of extrahepatic ducts. **Most common cause of neonatal cholestasis**.
Feeds and grows well, jaundice, **acholic stools**: investigate urgently.
**Ultrasound first** (also finds choledochal cyst). Biopsy: duct proliferation, inflammation, fibrosis, bile plugs. **Gold standard: intraoperative cholangiogram**.
**Kasai before 60 days** gives the best flow, poor after 90 days.

sections.title: Congenital hepatic fibrosis and Alagille
notes: Congenital hepatic fibrosis: autosomal recessive, with **autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease**. Presents with **portal hypertension and varices**.

**Alagille**: autosomal dominant **JAG1**. **Paucity of bile ducts** (cholestasis), **peripheral pulmonary stenosis**, **butterfly vertebrae**, **posterior embryotoxon**, broad forehead with pointed chin.

sections.title: Hepatomegaly and its workup
notes: Newborn liver edge over **3.5 cm** below the costal margin, child over **2 cm**.
Causes: hepatitis (viral, autoimmune, drugs like acetaminophen), Wilson, Budd-Chiari, fatty liver, heart failure, storage disease (glycogen, mucopolysaccharidoses).
Labs: CBC, retic, chemistry, fractionated bilirubin, ESR, GGT, **PT**, hepatitis serology, alpha-1 antitrypsin, AFP, **ceruloplasmin**, ANA, anti-smooth muscle, anti-LKM, sweat chloride, lipids.

sections.title: Hepatitis A
notes: Fecal-oral (food, travel). Often asymptomatic, then malaise, fever, vomiting, jaundice. Supportive, **avoid acetaminophen**.
Vaccine at **12 and 18 months** (2 doses 6 months apart). Travellers over 1 year: vaccine before travel. **Under 1 year: immunoglobulin**.
Post-exposure immunoglobulin for long exposures (daycare, household), not school or work.

sections.title: Hepatitis B and its serology
notes: Blood and sexual spread, **not by kissing, hugging or sharing utensils**.
**HBsAg**: infection. **Anti-HBc**: infection. **Anti-HBs alone: vaccinated**. **Anti-HBs plus anti-HBc: past infection, resolved**.
**HBeAg**: replication and infectivity. Anti-HBe: improving, the goal of therapy.

sections.title: Hepatitis B treatment and prevention
notes: Supportive. Interferon or lamivudine are approved.
**Routine vaccination**. Kids with hepatitis B can attend school or daycare unless they bite.
**HBIG** for babies of HBsAg-positive mothers. Preterms under 2 kg need a **4th dose**. Low titres after vaccination are still protected.

sections.title: Hepatitis C
notes: Leads to cirrhosis and cancer. Genotype 1 is hardest to treat.
Associated: **membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis**, ITP.
Babies of infected mothers: only **5% infected**, 30% of those clear it. **HCV RNA at 1 to 2 months**, or **anti-HCV at 18 months or later** (maternal antibody before). Direct-acting antivirals.

sections.title: Autoimmune hepatitis
notes: Presents like viral hepatitis with **negative viral serology**. Splenomegaly, other autoimmune disease in the family.
AST and ALT can be in the thousands, **high gamma globulin with low albumin**, prolonged PT.
Antibodies: **anti-smooth muscle, ANA, anti-LKM**. Treat with **prednisone and azathioprine**, fast response.
